Carol Shillabeer joined as chief executive of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board in May 2023

The chief executive of Wales's largest health board will no longer take up a new post in England, following a damning review of her current organisation's leadership.

Carol Shillabeer, who has been Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board's chief executive since May 2023, had been due to lead the Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Trust in England in the new year.

But a review into the Welsh health board found that, in some parts, targets and money had a "greater priority for senior management than the quality and safety of care".

The Lancashire and South Cumbria Trust said the "seriousness of the findings" could not be ignored and Shillabeer made the "personal decision" to withdraw from the role.

Dyfed Edwards, chair of Betsi Cadwaladr health board, confirmed Shillabeer would leave her current post on 3 January 2027. He thanked her for her service and wished her well for the future.

Confirming Shillabeer's withdrawal from the role, the Lancashire and South Cumbria Trust said it had "taken our time to carefully consider the situation and discuss the matter" with her.

"Carol feels that this is the best course of action for the sake of the patients, our communities, and LSCFT staff."

"We agree with her decision and wish her the best for the future," it added.

A spokesperson said that a board of trustees would consider the next steps regarding the appointment of a new chief executive.

Shillabeer spent three and a half years leading the health board, which covers all of north Wales. She was appointed after the Welsh government put it into "special measures" for the second time in its history.

It has been under the highest level of oversight due to concerns about care quality, patient safety and leadership .

Betsi Cadwaladr health board has been beset by problems since its inception in 2009

The independent review published on Tuesday found the health board lacked "the organisational conditions necessary to reliably deliver and sustain improvement".

It concluded that senior leadership was "immature and ineffective", with weak senior management putting the quality of patient care at risk.

It also said the health board had a "dedicated and loyal" workforce, with a "high level of expertise" across many services, as well as the capacity to provide strong local services.

The health board apologised and said it now needed to concentrate on improving its leadership and allowing its staff to "flourish".

Responding to the document, Health Minister, Mabon ap Gwynfor MS, rejected calls for "radical action or structural change".

Instead, he suggested that "stability" is needed following a period characterised by "too much change."

The Premier League heads into another big weekend and BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert Holly Shand gives her answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek 12.

Erling Haaland (£15.8m) has blanked in three consecutive games for Manchester City , who have taken just one point in this period. More than 100,000 managers have transferred Haaland out this week, despite him being the most owned player in the game. Form and fixtures collide, with league leaders Arsenal up next.

He has a good record against the Gunners, scoring in their last four Premier League meetings. Additionally, I believe Haaland will be the best captain pick in the game for his next three home games against Leeds United , Chelsea and Hull City so I recommend holding the highest-scoring forward in the game.

With Haaland's appeal dwindling this week, there are other options to consider across our squads. Bruno Fernandes (£11.6m) leads the data informed approach, as Manchester United entertain Brentford for Mauricio Pochettino's first game at Old Trafford. Are you brave enough to back the new manager bounce?

Elsewhere, Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) faces Coventry at home, scoring in three of his last five at Elland Road, while Nicolas Jackson (£7.5m) travels to Ipswich Town , with four goal involvements in four. Or could it be a week to back a defender with Brighton 's Maxim De Cuyper (£5.5m) ? He's the highest-scoring player in the game!

If you own four of more players from Arsenal and Manchester City , then there's a strong case to play the Free Hit in Gameweek 12 to avoid that fixture. Back Leeds and Brighton defences, at home to Coventry and Newcastle respectively with James Trafford (£5.1m) , Tarik Muharemovic (£5.1m) , Luka Vuskovic (£5.3m) and De Cuyper.

Liverpool are among the form sides, with Florian Wirtz (£7.4m) and Alexander Isak (£9.1m) worth considering. Wirtz has hit a double digit return in his last two games. There's also places in the midfield for top performers Marcus Tavernier (£6.8m) and Pascal Gross (£6.3m) .

Cole Palmer has just one goal in his last five games which has frustrated his owners, and he picked up a red card in that period too. Chelsea 's attack has struggled to find the same intensity with Joao Pedro out injured, scoring just three goals in this time.

While Palmer's time in our squads is coming to a close, he is nailed on for 90 minutes in a congested period of games, with Chelsea not involved in Europe. He deserves the benefit of the doubt with Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace up next. Liverpool in Gameweek 14 is the obvious exit point.

The news coming out of Arsenal is still mixed on the fitness of the highest-owned goalkeeper in the game David Raya (£6.3m) . We do know he is not believed to need surgery, which means he is not expected to be out long term. He's probably a hold.

If news arrives he will only miss Gameweek 12, you could Free Hit, or go without a goalkeeper if your substitute goalkeeper is non-playing. Spurs ' Antonin Kinsky (£4.4m) leads the way for possible back-ups, with games against Sunderland and Fulham in the immediate schedule.

It is worth noting there is just 48 hours between Gameweek 12 drawing to a close and the midweek Gameweek 13 deadline, coming on Tuesday, 1 December at 6:30pm GMT. Set those alarms so that you don't miss any action over the congestion in the next six weeks!

Be mindful that we might see increased rotation in the midweek rounds, particularly for wingers and full-backs. Those sides already involved in Europe are more likely to rotate, so having a strong bench in these instances could be key.

Also look out for players who are on four bookings, like Tavernier and Gross, as another yellow card could result in a one-match ban.

MN202611_1o1fihq8eyk.t:
Nessar Khawaja told almost 70,000 social media followers his network makes money from "desperate" customers

Organised networks of rogue plumbers and electricians have been scamming people on a large scale, a BBC investigation has found.

Nessar Khawaja, who used the online name ThatGuyNess, regularly posted TikTok videos showing his work as a plumber, explaining how he made thousands of pounds from "desperate" customers, and recruiting online to expand his network.

"Me and my team, we're top of the food chain," he said in one video.

The investigation found the 23-year-old is a key figure within an organised group that is systematically ripping off customers and teaching others to do the same.

The BBC put these allegations to Khawaja in writing. He denied any wrongdoing and said his social media posts were intended as light-hearted comedy that did not reflect how he operated in practice.

In a recorded phone call, Khawaja insisted he was an entertainer, was joking and that the BBC had "taken things out of context".

In another video, Khawaja made claims he had electricians working for him who made more than £40,000 a month.

"I've got 100-120 engineers. Imagine how much money I am making them and making from them," he said.

One of Khawaja's associates told an undercover BBC journalist during a secretly-recorded recruitment call that engineers working for them had to hand over 60% from every job to the network.

After being approached for comment, TikTok said it banned the account for "breaching its rules on fraud and scams".

Clive was billed £9,153 by a suspected rogue trader for fitting an outdoor socket in his garden

Trading Standards said the average rogue trader call-out scam now costs the victim about £10,000.

Clive, who lives in London, is undergoing treatment for cancer.

He said he had felt forced to pay the rogue trader who came to his home and charged £9,153 for installing an outdoor socket to fit garden lights he already owned.

An independent electrical expert told the BBC the job had not been done properly, was left in an unsafe state and should have cost no more than £250.

Clive said he no longer feels safe in his home.

He explained how he had searched for a local electrician on Google when his usual tradesperson was unavailable and came across Chriss Electrician Ltd.

Clive said the engineer spent about two hours at the property before presenting him with the bill.

He added he had felt pressured into paying as the work had already been completed.

He went to his local bank branch to move money between accounts before returning home and making the payment through the engineer's portable card reader.

Despite his doubts about the costs, Clive said he had feared what might happen if he refused to pay.

"If I hadn't paid him, I thought something might happen," he said.

"When people come to the door now, I think, 'Oh God, who's that?' I don't feel safe any more."

While the BBC has not seen evidence that Khawaja controls or runs this company, it has established the following:

Companies House places Chriss Electrician Ltd at an address in Ilford

Khawaja appears as the listed director of two dissolved companies inside that same building, one inside the very same flat

Khawaja's company First Choice Maintenance 24/7 Limited was registered 22 days before Chriss Electrician Ltd was incorporated and registered at the same flat as its address.

The BBC contacted Chriss Electrician Ltd for comment but it has not responded.

Khawaja denied having any connection with Chriss Electrician Ltd.

Clive was refunded by his bank after it was contacted by the BBC. The bank said it had done so as a "gesture of goodwill".

'I was threatened with rape after locksmith scam'

Secret filming catches locksmith charging 10 times quote

Like Clive, another man, who the BBC has named as Tom, felt he had no choice but to settle the bill when he mistakenly called a rogue trader to his property in Essex after finding a leak.

He says he was initially quoted £49 over the phone after calling a listing at the top of Google purporting to be an established business.

But on arrival, the plumber increased the call-out fee to £250 and the costs kept on climbing.

"He charged us for the first load of repairs, and then the second load with the water cylinder. Basically, he was running my taps constantly saying, 'Look, it's coming out this hot', which caused me to panic."

By the end, the plumber presented a bill for £6,237.60.

"I noticed afterwards that the invoice said Ibby & Co. Ltd. That was when alarm bells started ringing because I had never heard of that company. It wasn't the company I called out, essentially."

Tom called another plumber to get a second opinion and was told the work that was completed should have cost no more than £1,000.

When Tom called the company to complain, he received threats from an unknown man. The call was recorded and the BBC heard threats including: "We'll show up at your house. And we're gonna be sleeping there for months."

Ibrahim Nazir, the plumber who came to Tom's property and the listed director of Ibby and Co Ltd, has been contacted by the BBC for comment but has not responded.

Sources close to Khawaja place Nazir inside the same network.

Khawaja said he did not know anything about the job involving Tom and stated Nazir was not in his employ.

Monetising vulnerability and desperation is key to the rogue trader business model, insiders say.

One insider forwarded the BBC a script being circulated by a different rogue trader network recruiting young men for commission-based work.

The document tells recruits to hike prices if children or pets are trapped inside and even instructs them to fake picking a lock for seven minutes before drilling it.

Lee, not his real name, spent a year working for Khawaja as a plumber until, he says, his conscience got the better of him.

"It got a bit too much for me," he said. "I didn't like scamming people. So, I left.

"I've worked for London's biggest plumbing company and, no word of a lie, this lot have more jobs. They're giants."

Rather than relying on solid reputations and recommendation, rogue traders rely on search engine traffic.

They either pay to get their details at the top of Google, which means they are seen first, or they mimic the names of reputable companies by making tiny changes to the business name.

Reached by the BBC's undercover journalist posing as a plumber seeking to work with them, one of Khawaja's associates said: "We're a lead company. We'll send you jobs, and then you go to the jobs.

"We sort the jobs through online advertisement. Usually we'll try and get emergencies so we can charge more. You make up the pricing."

The associate told the undercover reporter they had to charge in the region of £400 for every job, regardless of what work was actually needed.

Both Clive and Tom reported what happened to the Metropolitan Police and Essex Police.

Khawaja said he was not a party to the phone call with the undercover journalist and could not comment on its contents.

He said the alleged statements did not reflect how he operates.

He separately told the BBC in the recorded phone call: "You guys should know I am an entertainer and you guys are taking it out of context."

"I am clearly joking and I'm entertaining and I am engaging with the comments, it is not literal," he added.

He said the right of reply sent to him by the BBC contained "false information which has nothing to do with me".

TikTok said its community guidelines were "clear" and did not "allow any attempts to scam, trick or defraud people".

The firm said in the three months up to June 2026, it had removed 99.2% of content found to be in breach of its "policies on fraud and scams... before it was reported to us".

The BBC put questions to Google including why rogue traders were able to advertise on its platform. It did not answer specific questions, but a Google spokesperson said: "We have strict ads policies that govern the types of ads and advertisers we allow on our platforms.

"Keeping our users and partners safe is our top priority and we invest heavily in the enforcement of our policies.

"We have a team of thousands working around the clock to create and enforce our policies at scale."

Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam said the postponement was driven by factors including final reasons

Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have postponed elections scheduled for next week by two years, delaying the return to civilian rule.

Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam announced in a decree that the presidential and parliamentary elections, originally due on 6 December, would now take place on 26 November 2028.

The announcement came exactly a year after the military seized power, promising to return the country to civilian rule within 12 months.

In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of electoral preparations had found that there were insufficient "technical, material and financial conditions" to hold the polls as planned.

It said the delay would provide more time to ensure the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities.

The presidency also reiterated its commitment to holding the country's first-ever local government elections but gave no date for the vote.

Gen N'Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025.

The coup took place three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were due to be announced.

Both Embaló and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory.

Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing an interest in contesting the elections.

Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974.

MN202611_u0123oszia.t:
Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road

Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT).

Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads.

At stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season.

As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift.

The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's.

They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline.

Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990.

Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record.

"We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he said.

"We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter.

"It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game."

Robbie Savage: 'We want to turn the county blue'

The victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February.

"This game is at the top of the mountain," he said.

"No doubt about it. The players will be up for it, we've shown them videos of the previous games, we've got fans sending messages.

"We're doing everything we can to make them realise how big this game is. It's not another game, it's the derby. A great game.

"Neil knows what it means. We're two passionate managers. He's done far better than me as a manager so far, so hats off to him. But we both want to win.

"They will bring 1,600 fans and we need to show Cambridge that we want to county to be blue."

Neil Harris: 'We'll attack the game like no other'

While this derby is new territory for Savage, Harris comes armed with the memory of defeat in his only previous taste of the tie in a season than ultimately ended with relegation for the U's.

After securing a return to the third-tier in 2025-26 - and having made a competitive start to this campaign - there is no shortage of motivation to deliver a long-awaited win for his side.

"It is a one-off fixture," he told BBC Look East.

"There is a slightly different feel and mentality to it, but it means a hell of a lot to a hell of a lot of people.

"It means a lot to get bragging rights over a direct opponent. It's important to get back to our highest standards."

Posh have lost just one of their past 12 league games against Cambridge United, winning their past four in succession.

But with Savage's side in a precarious league position, there is optimism among fans that their 36-year long wait to celebrate a league win at London Road could finally arrive.

"It's about playing with heart and emotion, but brains as well," added Harris.

"We understand the importance of the fixture, I understand it as a driven manager. It's about trying to make sure we make our fans proud."

Millions of women and girls remain unprotected in South Asia because of inadequate laws to deal with marital rape

Failure to fully criminalise marital rape leaves millions of women and girls unprotected in eight South Asian countries, where intimate partner violence is 35% higher than the global average, says a new study.

More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia - India, Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh - remain among the three dozen countries which haven't.

The only South Asian country where rape within marriage attracts the same penalty as any other rape is The Maldives.

Nepal and Bhutan have criminalised marital rape, but apply lesser penalties, says the study by Samaj, a coalition of women's rights groups in the region.

India is among the three dozen countries where marital rape is still not outlawed

South Asia's marital rape laws largely stem from British colonial rule, says Ranjeeta Silwal of Equality Now, a global women's rights group part of Samaj.

The law, dating to 1860 in India and Bangladesh and 1885 in Sri Lanka, lists exceptions to rape - including sex by a man with his adult wife.

Campaigners say the law is outdated and forced sex is rape, regardless of the perpetrator. Experts warn marital sexual violence harms women's physical, psychological, emotional and sexual well-being.

More than 100 countries have criminalised marital rape, including the UK, which changed its law in 1991. But the exemption remains in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

In India, growing clamour to criminalise rape within marriage

Marital rape: Delhi high court gives split verdict

India government says criminalising marital rape 'excessively harsh'

Pakistan removed the marital rape exception in 2006, but no higher court has confirmed that rape laws apply within marriage. A recent high court ruling, meanwhile, granted husbands broad immunity for non-consensual sex.

Since returning to power in 2021, the Taliban have steadily dismantled women's protections in Afghanistan.

A new penal code introduced in January made matters worse, Silwal says. Under it, a husband can be prosecuted for violence against his wife only if he causes a broken bone, open wound or severe bruising. Even then, he faces just 15 days in prison if convicted.

Unsurprisingly, the code makes no mention of marital rape. But its narrow definition of punishable violence effectively denies women protection against it.

Intimate partner violence is much higher than the global average in South Asian countries

"The idea comes from the belief that consent for sex is implied in marriage, that marriage is a threshold where consent ends," Silwal told the BBC.

"But it shows a lack of awareness, it shows we are still treating women as property, that we are still very patriarchal."

The report comes amid renewed debate over marital rape across the region.

In India, 10 petitions challenging the law are pending before the Supreme Court, which is due to begin final hearings on 9 December.

Courts have delivered contradictory rulings over the years, with some judges acknowledging the law's archaic nature and urging parliament to criminalise marital rape.

There was outrage last year when a court let go a man whose wife had died after he brutally raped her.

But the Indian government, religious organisations and men's rights activists have opposed petitions in the top court, saying criminalisation of marital rape would be " excessively harsh ".

India refuses to criminalise marital rape. This new series shines a light on it

India anger as judge frees man accused of raping wife who then died

Rights groups in Bangladesh have also challenged the marital rape exception, arguing it violates constitutional rights to life, liberty and protection from torture and cruel treatment, the report says.

"Those who oppose criminalising marital rape say it would undermine the family unit and break them apart. And family is very important in our countries," Silwal says.

"They say it will affect our religious and cultural values and worry that there would be false accusations against men."

Also a change in law, she says, may not necessarily mean justice for survivors.

Silwal points to Bhutan where marital rape is a criminal offence but it's treated as a petty misdemeanour and is punishable by one month to one year.

In Nepal, the punishment for rape is between six and 20 years, but it's only up to five years for a husband who rapes his wife.

Mu rwego rwogukomeza kubungabunga ibudukikije, harwanywa isuri ndetse n'ibiza biterwa n'imtuzure y'imvura, binyuze mu bufatanye muri Banki ya Kigali, mu ishami ryayo ridahararanira inyungu BK Foundation hamwe n'umuryango utegamiye kuri Leta uteza imbere abaturage (RWARRI) hatewe ibiti by'ubwoko butandukanye mu karere ka Rubavu. Umuyobozi w'umuryango nyarwanda utegamiye kuri Leta uteza imbere abaturage, Uwizeye Belange avuga ko, ngo binyuze mu bufatanye bwa BK Foundation n'uyu muryango, bataganyaga gutera ibiti bingana n'ibihumbi mirongo irindwi, mu turere twa Rubavu na Rutsiro, ariko ko, ngo umubare wiyongeye, aho ibiti bari butere muri utu, turere wavuye kuri ku bihumbi mirongo irindwi, ukagera kuri mirongo icyenda.

Uretse kuba intego yo gutera ibi biti, ari ukubungabunga idukikije no kurwanya isuri aho yagiye igaragara, Karangwayire Ingrid umunyamabanga nshingabikorwa wa Bk Foundation, avuga ko, impamvu bahisemo gutera ibiti ku musozi wa Nengo, ngo ari uko wari waramaze kwangizwa n'isuri, yongeraho ko, kandi n'ahandi bazabitera, ari ahari isuri cyangwa aho bigaragara ko, hashobora kwibasirwa na yo.

Gahunda y'ubufwtanye bwa Bk foundation n'umuryango utegamiye kuri Leta uteza imbere abaturage RWARRI, ni uko bagba gukomeza gutera ibiti by'ubwoko butandukanye, harimo n'iby'imbuto, byose hamwe bikagera kuri miliyoni.

MN202611_es02zuj4ug.t:
The Uganda People’s Defense Forces have begun preparing to withdraw from Lubero city of North Kivu province saying the Allied Democratic Front rebels are nolonger in the area.

Since January 2025, the UPDF has been maintaining security of Lubero town under a joint military cooperation with the Congolese military code named operation Shujaa launched in November 2021 to hunt down the ADF rebels allied to Islamic State terrorist organisation.

According to Kampala, Ugandan Army is scheduled to handover responsibility for security in the town to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC).

According to a statement released this Friday, November 27, 2026, in Kampala, the withdrawal will begin within the next two weeks.

Kinshasa Questions Uganda’s Relations With Kabila-led FRN Rebels

Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, DRC’s Foreign Affairs Minister has tasked Uganda government to clarify it’s diplomatic status with DRC.

Early this week, Uganda’s head of diplomatic mission in Kinshasa was summoned to explain statements made by Uganda’s military chief, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba.

Gen. Muhoozi posted comments on X appearing to back the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) rebels and signaling Ugandan forces would not oppose their advance on Walikale.

“The Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) will soon withdraw its forces out of Lubero Town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, handing over its security to the Congolese armed forces FARDC,” said Col. Chris Magezi the Acting Director Defence Public Information of Defense Ministry.

He added, “UPDF withdrawal from the town located in the North Kivu province will start in the next two weeks. The UPDF has operated in the area since January 2025 to counter fleeing Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) remnants that sought to escape pressure of joint military operations in North Kivu and Ituri provinces of eastern DRC.”

MN202611_14zq3qji809.t:
Rwanda has received 106 of its citizens who returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where they had been living in forests, through the Rusizi I border crossing on Thursday, November 26, 2026.

The group comprises 28 women and 78 children, who crossed into the country from the neighbouring DRC.

The returnees were received at the Rusizi I border post, which connects the two countries, as authorities continue to facilitate the return of Rwandan citizens from across the border.

The group includes no men, with children accounting for the largest share of those who returned.

Rusizi District Mayor, Sindayiheba Phanuel, welcomed the returnees and thanked them for choosing to come back, assuring them that local authorities would support their reintegration into society.

He said misinformation about the situation in their home country had previously discouraged some from returning.

“While they were there, they had been receiving false information about Rwanda, but after learning the truth, they decided to return. That is what we thank them for,” Sindayiheba said.

The Mayor also assured the returnees that children who had missed out on education while living in difficult conditions in the forests would be supported to access schooling and other essential services.

Following their arrival, the 106 returnees were transferred to the Nyarushishi Temporary Reception Centre in Nkungu Sector, Rusizi District, where they are expected to spend three weeks receiving basic assistance and civic education.

They will also undergo documentation procedures before being reunited with relatives and families they left behind when they fled to the DRC.

The latest arrivals add to the growing number of Rwandans returning from eastern DRC amid continued efforts to facilitate the voluntary repatriation of citizens who have been living in difficult conditions across the border.

MN202611_k66ptrprod.t:
The Government has approved a new investment agreement with BRALIRWA Plc to establish a beverage manufacturing plant in Rwamagana Industrial Park, alongside plans to introduce mobile number portability, allowing subscribers to change telecommunications providers without losing their existing phone numbers.

The decisions were adopted during a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame at Village Urugwiro on November 26, 2026.

The proposed BRALIRWA investment is among several projects endorsed by Cabinet, including an agreement with EH Venture Capital Rwanda Limited to develop Phase II of Kigali Financial Square.

Cabinet also approved an investment agreement with SteelRwa Industries Ltd to establish a steel manufacturing plant and expand steel-related operations.

On telecommunications, the meeting approved a framework allowing subscribers to switch between mobile network operators while retaining their existing numbers.

The initiative is also intended to facilitate the transfer of mobile money accounts and related services, strengthen competition among operators and improve service delivery.

In another development, Cabinet approved an agreement between the Government and the African Wildlife Foundation to support the restoration and expansion of Gishwati-Mukura National Park.

It also endorsed a forest conservation cooperation agreement with the Government of Indiana in the United States.

The meeting further approved the launch of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign, running from November 25 to December 10, 2026.

Additionally, Kigali will host the sixth edition of Hanga Pitchfest on December 2, 2026, bringing together innovators and entrepreneurs to showcase their ideas and compete for opportunities to advance their businesses.

The decisions cover a range of priorities, including industrial investment, telecommunications, environmental conservation, gender-based violence prevention and entrepreneurship.

MN202611_qnwlk7pi11.t:
The planned withdrawal will end Uganda's nearly two-year campaign against ADF militants in Lubero

Uganda has announced plans to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.

The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.

The announcement comes days after DR Congo summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over controversial social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the son of President Yoweri Museveni.

The Ugandan military did not give a reason for the withdrawal or say whether it was linked to the diplomatic row.

What are Ugandan forces doing in DR Congo?

The Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) were deployed to Lubero to pursue fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) Islamist group fleeing joint military operations elsewhere in eastern DR Congo.

The ADF, which originated in Uganda in the 1990s, is affiliated to the Islamic State and has been blamed for numerous deadly attacks on civilians in both countries.

Uganda first deployed troops to eastern DR Congo under the current joint military campaign in November 2021, following a series of bomb attacks in the Ugandan capital, Kampala.

Ugandan army spokesperson Col Chris Magezi said that the joint military campaign, known as Operation Shujaa, would continue elsewhere in DR Congo.

The planned withdrawal applies only to Lubero town.

Five years into the joint offensive, the ADF remains DR Congo's deadliest armed group, despite a significant decline in its activities in Uganda, according to the conflict monitoring organisation Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (Acled).

John Ngono, Acled's DR Congo analyst, said the group was killing an average of four civilians a day and had expanded into previously unaffected parts of eastern DR Congo.

He said the findings suggested that "Operation Shujaa may have improved security in Uganda while shifting the geographical impact of violence within the DRC".

Acled says the group has not carried out an attack in Uganda since June 2025, but its growing interest in mineral resources in DR Congo could help finance its operations and sustain its ability to threaten both countries.

The planned withdrawal comes amid strained relations between Uganda and DR Congo, despite years of close military co-operation.

Earlier this week, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to endorse a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo, threatening that Ugandan troops would seize it themselves if the rebels failed to do so.

The Congolese foreign ministry described his remarks as "particularly serious" and demanded that Uganda clarify its official position and take steps to prevent similar incidents.

Gen Kainerugaba also defended Uganda's military presence in eastern DR Congo, insisting it was driven by security concerns.

The planned withdrawal comes amid renewed fighting between Congolese forces and rebels in the wider Lubero territory, raising fresh concerns about the safety of civilians.

Eastern DR Congo has endured decades of conflict involving dozens of armed groups, with millions of people forced to flee their homes.

MN202611_1w1ctyt5qfn.t:
Newcastle United defender Sven Botman has been banned from driving

Premier League footballer Sven Botman has been banned from driving after being caught using his mobile phone at the wheel.

The Newcastle United centre-back pleaded guilty to using a handheld mobile phone while using a motor vehicle on a road at Newcastle Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.

The 26-year-old was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued.

He was fined £900 and ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 victim surcharge, the MoJ said.

Botman was driving a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone.

The Dutchman changed his plea from not guilty to guilty at his court appearance on Wednesday, the MoJ confirmed.

Newcastle United signed Botman from Lille in 2022. He has made nine appearances so far this season, scoring one goal.

Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits the US

Hundreds of thousands of people are without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

Eastern areas were lashed on Thursday by a powerful storm which brought high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. Pennsylvania remained the state worst hit by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring site Poweroutage.us.

Conditions are forecast now to improve, though the National Weather Service (NWS) cautions that it will take some time. The West Coast has also been affected by its own storms.

Flight disruption also persists, with hundreds more delays and cancellations reported on Friday - which is expected to be another busy travel day.

More than 2,500 flights within, into or out of the US were delayed on Thursday, and more than 450 were cancelled, according to Flightaware.com.

One passenger told the BBC he had been stuck at New York's LaGuardia Airport for 13 hours while trying to fly to see friends in Chicago for Thanksgiving.

Beyond the travel disruption, impacts were widespread across the East Coast, and US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds.

Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds, while waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.

On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport.

The number of homes reporting power cuts peaked at close to a million on Thursday evening - with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey badly affected.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said utility providers were working tirelessly to restore power. In Maryland, almost two million customers were asked by authorities to limit their water consumption to essential use only due to "intermittent power disruptions".

Parts of eastern states are under states of emergency, including New York. Organisers of New York City's annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have also postponed the iconic event to Saturday.

Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather

On the West Coast, the concern was for exceptionally high tides and the associated risk of flooding.

Both San Diego and Los Angeles reported a high tide of over 8ft (2.4m) earlier this week, and beach-goers were advised to avoid coastal areas.

Watch: Man and dog narrowly escape powerful king tide in Oregon

Train services along the Amtrak Pacific Surfliner, which runs along the California coastline, cancelled several trains due to "washout conditions from high tides", the company shared on social media.

Dramatic footage from Oregon showed a man and a dog being swept into the sea by a fierce, so-called king tide - but both escaped unharmed, police said.

FedEx aircraft FedEx plane sends dirt flying while overshooting Miami runway dirt in the air while overshooting Miami runway

In Miami, some travel delays persisted into Thursday after a FedEx plane overshot the runway the night before, which prompted the closure of all but one runway at the airport for a brief period.

A statement FedEx provided to US media confirmed that one of its flights had "experienced an issue upon landing". No injuries were reported, and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating what happened.

An airport employee who spoke anonymously to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, raised the possibility that rainy conditions had been a factor.

The American Automobile Association (AAA) predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for the Thanksgiving holiday over a seven-day period.

MN202611_1t0tapdl83z.t:
Fan violence marred the tie at the Stade Velodrome

Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.

There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok.

In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters.

With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters.

They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions.

"Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds."

Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished".

According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims.

Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media.

"The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added.

"Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety."

Fan violence mars Marseille-Levski Sofia match

Police response to Besiktas fans' pro-Palestine banner 'unacceptable'

Sunderland held by Polish side Jagiellonia

Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents".

The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests".

Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0.

"It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez

Marseille boss Bruno Genesio added: "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable."

Besiktas fans clash with Georgian police at their game against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva

Meanwhile, the Turkish Football Federation has strongly condemned the "unacceptable" actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva.

Besiktas say they have lodged a complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by Georgian police.

The match had been moved from Istanbul to Batumi, Georgia for safety and security reasons but had to be suspended in the 25th minute after clashes involving Besiktas supporters and local police.

Both the officiating team and the Besiktas players left the field, but play was able to resume 30 minutes later.

"We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match," said a statement from the Turkish federation.

Turkish outlet NTV reported that Georgian police had gone into the stands and used pepper spray on the Besiktas fans.

The report added that there were anti-Israeli chants from the Turkish fans and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters to try to calm matters before play restarted.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's minister of foreign affairs, spoke to his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili following the incident.

"All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights," a Turkish foreign ministry source said.

At Sunderland, there were crowd disturbances after Jagiellonia Bialystok fans were found in areas of the Stadium of Light with home fans, despite Uefa having imposed an away supporter ban for the Europa League game.

Police and stewards attended some disruption early on during the match.

"In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and Uefa," said a Sunderland statement.

"Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.

"We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and we will review the circumstances surrounding their entry into the stadium."

MN202611_ajyll8ukyy.t:
With a win tonight, Tonda Eckert's Southampton would move to within four points of Kim Hellberg's Championship-leading Middlesbrough side

"I don't want to shut out the noise, we just need to know that it's coming and it's going to be electric."

The "noise" Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert refers to has been building over recent weeks, with 'Spygate' returning to the collective consciousness as Saints and Middlesbrough meet on Friday (20:00 GMT) for the first time since the scandal.

The most recent time they came face-to-face was in last season's Championship play-off semi-finals.

Saints ended up winning over the two legs, but were then expelled from the final having being caught spying on a Boro training session before the first match at the Riverside.

It turned into a five-month saga which started with a Saints performance analyst being photographed from behind a tree, and ended with Eckert being handed a suspended ban and fined £28,000.

The German head coach signed a new deal at Saints exactly a week ago and previously admitted the experience of Spygate had changed his life.

Now St Mary's awaits as the two sides will re-ignite their rivalry after a tough end to the last campaign for both.

Saints players felt aggrieved for not being allowed to feature in the play-off final, while Boro suffered the heartbreak of losing at Wembley, as Hull City won promotion to the Premier League.

"It's a massive game for both teams," former Nottingham Forest and Ipswich defender Luke Chambers told the 72+ podcast.

"Middlesbrough have bounced back tremendously well from the play-offs, the ups and downs, they didn't know if they were coming or going, and to go through that heartache of making the final and not getting over the line - credit to them.

"It will be an electric atmosphere and there will be added needle on the pitch, especially with some of the things that happened in the games between the two sides last season when the news broke out."

Hellberg reveals Eckert apology after Spygate

Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal

'It's changed my life' - Eckert on Spygate scandal

Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg had to be seperated during last season's play-off semi-final

Boro boss Kim Hellberg and Eckert both arrived at their respective clubs in November 2025 and have enjoyed plenty of success on the pitch over the past 12 months.

But following the 2-1 defeat in May's play-off semi-final second leg at St Mary's, Hellberg described it as "one of the toughest days" in his coaching career.

Although Friday's game promises to be filled with emotion on the pitch and in the stands, the two head coaches claim to have made up since the events of last season after Eckert called Hellberg to apologise over the summer.

"We spoke and he called me. I've always been a person who wants to give people a second chance," Hellberg told BBC Radio Tees.

"He has also gone though some things that have been very tough for him in terms of this which is something you don't wish anyone.

"I think in general for me it's overplayed. We have talked about it, everything has been sorted and now I'm looking forward to playing against a good side with a good manager and see how good we can be, and I'm really looking forward to it."

After Eckert took responsibility and apologised over the summer, both he and the club also expressed a desire to move on after the backing of the Saints board and owner Dragan Solak.

Some members of the Middlesbrough press have been robust and consistent in their strong criticism of Southampton and Eckert since Spygate first emerged.

Eckert had walked out of media conferences during the play-off semi-final following some stern questioning of him, while a piece was published on Thursday which questioned the German's character.

On Friday, Southampton published their own video , external on club channels, emotionally recalling the play-off campaign and how success was "ours... until it wasn't" before Boro "got another go", followed by footage of Oli McBurnie's winner for Hull at Wembley.

"People talk about last season, but we're focused on this one," narrates Southampton-based streamer Tyrone, over clips of goals from this season. "And now, here we are again; new hope, more reasons to believe, the same leader. We know all eyes are on us, and we're ready."

Southampton fan Rob Maddox echoed the emotions of both managers and felt that the majority of both fanbases want to now put the previous distaste behind them.

"There has been so much football since the play-off semi-final that I think both clubs are ready to get on with it now," he said.

"Some might look to hype the game up as a rivalry but I think the game should be looked at as two very good footballing sides going head to head.

"Of course there is going to be that little bit of spice and I'm sure we'll see it in the stands, but I hope that after the game we're talking about both teams showing off what they can do on the pitch."

Boro fan Jack McBride agreed that "Spygate's over and done with now" but admitted there was still a feeling of "bitterness" within the fanbases.

"I've seen some back and forth which is fun and all part of being a football fan, but there's also the other side of it which is bitter, twisted and they're still going on about it in a negative way," he told BBC Radio Tees.

"We had our chance and we didn't take it. Saints have had a four-point deduction, Tonda's been punished, we move on. Was it enough? Personally, I don't think that it was but we move on from it.

"This is a game we've all been looking to, and it was probably the first fixture that Boro and Saints fans were looking for.

"I think it's going to be quite a hostile atmosphere. I think Saints will be booing constantly and Boro fans will bring the noise as much as they can."

Some Southampton fans brought binoculars to the second leg of their play-off semi-final against Middlesbrough last season

Hellberg reflects on 'fantastic year' at Boro

The sides' latest showdown is not only a tasty encounter because of the fallout from Spygate, but also because two of the division's best teams will be going toe-to-toe.

Boro are top of the table and have the Championship's leading goalscorer in Will Lankshear , who has scored 14 times in 15 appearances.

The 21-year-old joined the club from Tottenham Hotspur over the summer for a fee that could rise to as high as £20m, following an impressive loan spell at Oxford United.

Meanwhile, Saints forward Cyle Larin has also been enjoying something of a prolific campaign himself, netting eight times in his 13 matches.

Eckert's side are sixth, but would be fourth and three points off Boro if not for the four-point deduction handed to them because of Spygate.

The two sides have the best home records so far this season and have both scored more than 30 goals each across their 17 matches played.

"Friday's a massive game. A massive football game before anything else," Boro midfielder Myles Peart-Harris told BBC Radio Tees.

"The rivalry we now have is even better so the boys are looking forward to Friday. Hopefully we play our football, stick to what we know and get a result, we're ready.

"We're more excited about the game of football because we know they like to play football, we like to play football, so I think tactically it's going to be a great time for everyone to watch and most importantly we can go there and get a win."

Former Reading and Leyton Orient midfielder Jobi McAnuff told the 72+ podcast: "What it boils down to is two of the best teams in the league this year.

"I think it'll be a cracking atmosphere and there will still be needle there because it was such a huge story, it was massive.

"The implications and fallout went on for months and I think that will add to it. It will be a fantastic spectacle and I hope this season we are talking about what happens on the pitch rather than what's happened off it."
