An official inspects the partially submerged tanker - the rescue operation is expected to be challenging

A tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel which capsized off the holiday island of Ibiza on Thursday will be towed to the port of Cartagena, officials in Spain say.

All 17 of the Malta-registered Med Emre's crew members were rescued but the chief engineer later died in hospital. Six people were treated for minor injuries.

There had been concerns of a major oil spillage in the western Mediterranean but an inspection showed that the ship's fuel tanks are intact. An investigation is under way into what happened.

The vessel had been travelling from Algeciras near Gibraltar to Barcelona and is expected to arrive in Cartagena on Monday in what is being seen as a challenging rescue operation.

In a statement on Friday, the Spanish transport ministry said the tanker would be towed to Cartagena "as it is the only one [port] that meets the technical requirements to carry out cargo extraction and repair work".

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told Cadena SER radio network he hoped the tanker could be taken to port "in the coming hours, in the coming days".

"The information suggests that, indeed... this leak is not happening", he added.

The Spanish authorities provided no details about how the diesel would be extracted.

Meanwhile, pictures have emerged showing emergency workers inspecting the tanker's hull off the Balearic Islands.

Any possible environmental damage is being assessed by air and pollution control vessel Clara Campoamor, which is owned by Spain's national maritime rescue service.

Elena Delgado, maritime captain of the port of Valencia, earlier told news agency AFP that a small slick which had formed around the vessel had "disappeared".

"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out.

Regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk as originally reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.

The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 28 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia.

Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call late on Wednesday, according to Spanish media.

Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle. It capsized in the early hours on Thursday.

Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.

In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline, in the country's north-west.

More than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil spilled into the sea.

MN202611_wuugbb28c5.t:
Ibi byatangajwe na Minisiteri y’Ingabo n’Ibikorwa by’Abahoze mu Ngabo za Uganda mu itangazo yasohoye ku wa Gatanu, tariki ya 27 Ugushyingo 2026, isubiza Guverinoma ya Repubulika Iharanira Demukarasi ya Congo iherutse guhamagaza Ambasaderi wa Uganda i Kinshasa kugira ngo asobanure amagambo yavuzwe na Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Umugaba Mukuru w’Ingabo za Uganda akaba n’Umujyanama Mukuru wa Perezida wa Uganda mu bikorwa byihariye.

Iryo tangazo rivuga ko ubuyobozi bwa RDC butishimiye amagambo Gen. Kainerugaba yavuze, arimo gushyigikira ifatwa ry’agace ka Walikale n’umutwe witwa FRN ukorera mu Burasirazuba bwa RDC, ndetse anagaragaza ko UPDF yiteguye gukurikirana Musa Baluku uyobora ADF kugeza aho yaba yihishe muri Isiro.

UPDF yavuze ko ibikorwa bihuriweho n’ingabo za Uganda n’iza RDC byo kurwanya ADF bikomeje, kandi ko igitutu izo ngabo zikomeje gushyira kuri uwo mutwe cyatumye abarwanyi bawo bacikamo amatsinda mato, bagahungira imbere mu gihugu.

Yongeyeho ko, ifatanyije n’Ingabo za RDC (FARDC), izakomeza gukurikirana ibisigisigi by’uwo mutwe n’abawuyobora aho bazajya bahungira hose. Ibi ngo biri mu masezerano y’ubufatanye azwi nka Operation Shujaa.

Muri iryo tangazo kandi Uganda yanagarutse ku yindi mitwe yitwaje intwaro ikorera muri ako Karere, irimo imitwe yitwaje intwaro ishyigikiwe na Leta ya RDC, izwi nka Wazalendo.

UPDF yavuze ko iyo mitwe yagiye igaba ibitero ku baturage batagira kirengera, birimo kwica abagore n’abana bo mu miryango y’Abahima n’Abatutsi mu Ntara ya Ituri na Kivu y'Amajyaruguru.

Ni nyuma y'uko Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, yatangaje ko Abahima n’Abatutsi bo muri Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC) abafata nk’abavandimwe be, ashimangira ko igihugu cye kizakomeza kubarengera.

Mu butumwa yanyujije ku rubuga nkoranyambaga rwa X, Gen. Kainerugaba yagize ati: “Mfata Abahima n’Abatutsi bo muri Congo nk’abavandimwe banjye. Kubarwanya ni kimwe no kurwanya Uganda. Tuzarengera abavandimwe bacu.”

Igisirikare cya Uganda cyavuze ko, hashingiwe ku mategeko mpuzamahanga agenga intambara no kurinda abasivili, gifite inshingano zo kurengera abaturage bashobora kugirwaho ingaruka n’ibi bikorwa, kandi ko kizakomeza kubikora igihe cyose bizaba bishoboka.

Ku rundi ruhande, Uganda yongeye gushimangira ko ishyigikiye ko amakimbirane yo mu Burasirazuba bwa RDC akemurwa mu mahoro, hagati ya Guverinoma ya RDC n’imitwe yitwaje intwaro ihanganye na yo.

Yavuze kandi ko itazashyigikira cyangwa ngo ifate byoroshye ibikorwa by’abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga bakorana n’imitwe yitwaje intwaro mu gutera ubwoba abaturage bo mu Burasirazuba bwa RDC.

MN202611_1nlbc5jm25h.t:
Banki ya Kigali (BK) ikomeje ibikorwa byo kwizihiza imyaka 60 imaze ikorera mu Rwanda, ishimangira ko izakomeza guhanga udushya no guteza imbere ikoranabuhanga mu kugeza serivisi z’imari ku bantu benshi no korohereza abakiliya kuyigeraho.

Ibi byagarutsweho ku mugoroba wo ku wa 26 Ugushyingo 2026, mu gikorwa cyiswe BK Digital Day 2026, cyabereye kuri Norrsken mu Mujyi wa Kigali. Cyahuje abashoramari mu ikoranabuhanga mu by’imari, abanyeshuri n’abayobozi bahagarariye inzego za Leta, urwego rw’imari n’urw’ikoranabuhanga.

Iki gikorwa gifite insanganyamatsiko igira iti “Imyaka 60 mu rugendo rwo guhanga udushya” (60 Years of Innovation), kikaba cyaranzwe no kumurika udushya n’ibisubizo by’ikoranabuhanga Banki ya Kigali yagiye iteza imbere mu rwego rwa serivisi z’imari.

Umuyobozi Mukuru wa Banki ya Kigali, Dr. Diane Karusisi, yavuze ko icyizere Abanyarwanda bagiriye iyi banki mu myaka 60 ishize ari cyo kintu cy’ingenzi cyayifashije gukomeza kugira uruhare mu iterambere ry’Igihugu. Yashimangiye ko izakomeza guhanga udushya no guteza imbere serivisi z’ikoranabuhanga kugira ngo irusheho kugera ku bakiliya bayo.

Yavuze ko mu myaka 60 ishize, Banki ya Kigali yakoranye n’Abanyarwanda bayigana bayizaniye intego n’inzozi zitandukanye, zirimo kuzigama amafaranga yo kwishyurira abana amashuri, kubaka amazu, kwagura ibikorwa by’ubucuruzi no gushora imari y’ahazaza habo.

Yasobanuye ko gufasha abo bakiliya kugera kuri izo ntego byasabye ko banki ihora ishaka uburyo bushya bwo kunoza serivisi no kugera ku bantu benshi kurushaho.

Ati: “Igisubizo kiroroshye. Si ubwinshi bw’umutungo n’imari dufite, si inyubako zacu, si amashami yacu, si ikoranabuhanga dukoresha. Ni icyizere Abanyarwanda bamaze imyaka mirongo itandatu batugirira, kandi icyo ni ikintu duha agaciro gakomeye cyane.”

Yongeyeho ko muri iki gihe ubuzima bwihuta, abantu batagifite umwanya wo kujya ku mashami ya banki gutegereza serivisi. Bityo, asanga ari ngombwa ko banki zibasanga aho bari kandi zikabaha serivisi igihe bazikeneye.

Yavuze ko ubu abakiliya bashobora gusaba inguzanyo cyangwa izindi serivisi z’imari bakoresheje telefoni zabo bari mu ngo, bakabona igisubizo mu gihe gito, aho gutegereza ibyumweru cyangwa amezi.

Ikoranabuhanga rigamije kugeza serivisi ku bantu benshi

Karusisi yavuze ko ikoranabuhanga ridakwiye gufatwa nk’uburyo bwo gukoresha ibikoresho bigezweho gusa, kuko rinagira uruhare mu kugabanya ikiguzi cyo gutanga serivisi no gutuma ibicuruzwa bya banki bigera ku bantu benshi.

Yagaragaje ko bidashoboka ko banki yafungura ishami muri buri mudugudu w’Igihugu, bityo ko gukoresha ikoranabuhanga ari bumwe mu buryo bwo korohereza abakiliya kuyigeraho. Icyakora, yibukije ko Banki ya Kigali ari ikigo cy’ubucuruzi, bityo ko igomba no gukorera inyungu zitezweho n’abashoramari n’abanyamigabane bayo.

Yashimangiye ko abakiliya bagomba kubona serivisi z’imari mu buryo bubaha agaciro, badakeneye kwinginga cyangwa kumva ko basabiriza kugira ngo bahabwe inguzanyo cyangwa izindi serivisi.

Mu bisubizo by’ikoranabuhanga byamuritswe muri BK Digital Day 2026 harimo urubuga rwa OpenAPI, rugamije gufasha abahanga udushya n’ibigo bikora ikoranabuhanga mu by’imari kubaka serivisi nshya bifashishije ibikorwaremezo Banki ya Kigali imaze imyaka yubaka.

Hagaragajwe kandi uburyo bushya butuma umuntu ufite konti bwite n’iyo mu bucuruzi ashobora kuzigeraho akoresheje porogaramu imwe, atiriwe ava kuri telefoni ngo ajye kuri mudasobwa cyangwa ikindi gikoresho.

Ubuyobozi bwa BK bwavuze ko ubu buryo bwashyizweho mu mezi make ashize, ariko ko bwifuje kubumurikira abantu benshi kugira ngo bamenye uko bukora n’icyo bubafasha.

Abakiriya ba Banki ya Kigali Bishimira Serivisi bahabwa

Mu buhamya bwatanzwe na Ishimwe Prince, umukiriya wa Banki ya Kigali wari uhagarariye Kaminuza y’Abadiventiste b’Umunsi wa Karindwi, yavuze ko gukoresha ikoranabuhanga byakemuye ibibazo byinshi by’abakiliya b’iyi banki.

Yagize ati: “Ndibuka kera njya kuri banki ngasanga abantu batonze umurongo, ariko uyu munsi nshobora gukora ibikorwa byose bya banki nicaye mu rugo. Ibi byakemuye ikibazo cy’ingendo ndende twakoraga, kuko serivisi zose zishobora kubonerwa kuri telefoni.”

Yashimye kandi porogaramu ya BK Advance, avuga ko izabafasha kubona amafaranga igihe bayakeneye mu buryo bwihuse. Yongeyeho ko ikoranabuhanga rya BK rifasha abakiliya kubona serivisi no kubona amafaranga vuba, bitabaye ngombwa ko bajya kuri banki gutonda umurongo.

Na Ahirwe Rutayisire Tesi Keny, na we umukiriya wa Banki ya Kigali, yavuze ko ikoranabuhanga iyi banki ikoresha rifasha abakiliya kubona serivisi mu buryo bwihuse kandi bwizewe.

Yagize ati: “Banki ya Kigali ifite ikoranabuhanga riri ku rwego rwo hejuru, kandi tuba twizeye umutekano w’amafaranga yacu.”

Rutayisire asanga izindi banki zo mu Rwanda hari byinshi zakwigira kuri Banki ya Kigali, birimo korohereza abakiliya hifashishijwe ikoranabuhanga no gucunga neza umutekano w’amafaranga baba barayibikije.

Wesley Fofana has made 10 appearances for Chelsea this season.

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League game at Nottingham Forest .

The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released.

In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool .

Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated".

But Fofana endured a difficult time in his side's trip to Forest as supporters made their feelings known.

After Chelsea went behind to a brilliant volley from Igor Jesus in the fifth minute, Fofana also conceded a penalty for the home side's second goal from Morgan Gibbs-White in the 51st minute.

He was booked for the foul on Liam Delap in the box, and then replaced by Levi Colwill in the 56th minute - just after Emmanuel Emegha had pulled a goal back for the visitors - before Gibbs-White made it 3-1 in the 72nd minute.

Meanwhile, Nani has moved to defend Fofana, saying the player was "clearly" not happy during the interview and admitted he had to perform better.

Fofana also explained he opted to take a penalty against Liverpool as one of the senior players on the pitch, having joined in a £75m move from Leicester City in 2022.

But he confessed football had reached a stage where he was "more unhappy than happy", before recovering physically and mentally.

The release of the interview has coincided with the club's poor run of form, with Chelsea losing 4-1 at home to Leeds United last weekend to make it three defeats in four matches.

The defence, in particular, has come in for criticism, with the Blues one of four clubs to have conceded more than 20 goals in the Premier League after 11 matches.

Having been subjected to racist abuse in the past, Fofana spoke about handling comments during a club-organised interview on this summer's pre-season tour of Asia.

He is understood to be one of the highest earners at Stamford Bridge.

Canadian prosecutors are seeking a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries.

Kenneth Law pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada, though he has admitted to causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.

The 61-year-old will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths under a plea deal which saw Canadian authorities withdraw more serious charges of murder.

During Friday's sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, prosecutors stressed that many of his victims were young and struggling with mental distress.

If Law receives the prosecution's recommended sentence, he would serve just under 20 years in prison, after accounting for credit for time served since his May 2023 arrest.

As she sought to make her case in court on Friday, Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty described Law as a predator taking advantage of "vulnerable people".

"What they needed was help. But what they found was Mr Law and his products for death," Doherty said.

She also said Law's motives were financial.

"If people could pay, he sold it to them. There's no discussion or inquiries or anything going on whereby Mr Law would have any ability to appreciate the circumstances of the individual he was dealing with," she said.

Law's defence lawyer, Matthew Gourlay, countered those claims, arguing that his client was not responsible for many of their battles with mental illness.

He said Law held a "misguided belief" he was helping his victims.

"Each of these incidents is its own unique tragedy," Gourlay said. "Mr Law may be a common denominator between them, but Mr Law was not the cause of the struggles and hardships that caused all these victims to seek out his products in the first place."

Law's defence attorney has asked the court to give him a 12-year sentence.

The sentencing hearing on Friday followed an emotional few days of testimony in September, when grieving family members and friends told the court of the pain Law had caused.

Those impact statements will be taken into account at sentencing, which is due at a later date.

Authorities said the former chef sold about 1,200 packages of toxic substances to recipients - who he met in online suicide forums - in 40 countries, roughly a quarter of which were sent to the UK.

If you or anyone you know has been affected by the issues raised in this article, details of organisations offering information are available at BBC Action Line

MN202611_4y3h3tzghj.t:
Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea at the City Ground for the first time since 1997.

Igor Jesus' brilliant volley opened the scoring after just five minutes, before Gibbs-White struck twice in the second half as Chelsea were consigned to a fourth defeat in five matches.

Forest ran out 3-2 winners despite Emmanuel Emegha twice pulling goals back.

Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Matz Sels: The Belgian goalkeeper could do little about Emegha's goal but did not need to make many saves. 6

Jair Cunha : Cunha made one brilliant last-ditch tackle in the second half as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. 7

Nikola Milenkovic : The Serbian was solid in the middle of the back three but otherwise unremarkable. 7

Murillo : The Brazilian centre-back made a host of important tackles and no-nonsense clearances throughout. He set the tone for a physical display and had a powerful volley saved. 7

Daniel Munoz : A typically energetic presence on the right, he also set up the opening goal. 7

James McAtee : The midfielder was good in possession but his shots lacked threat. His set-piece delivery was also poor. He did, however, win a few fouls for his team to take the pressure off. 7

Xaver Schlager : The combative midfielder set the tone early by winning the ball back in Chelsea 's half on multiple occasions. He screened the backline well as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. His wonderful pass through the eye of the needle created Forest's third. 9

Neco Williams : The Welshman battled hard with Pedro Neto in a tactical contest that ended with both players emerging with credit. 7

Igor Jesus : His sensational first-time volley opened the scoring just five minutes into the match, while the rest of his play was neat and tidy. 8

Morgan Gibbs-White : The forward scored his first goal in 11 games against Chelsea from the penalty spot in the second half. He took that chance and then another when played through by Schlager. 8

Liam Delap : The former Chelsea striker proved his worth to Forest by leading the line brilliantly, carrying a threat, looking dangerous in transition and ultimately winning a penalty for his side. 8

Subs not used: John Victor, Netz, Diomande, Yates, Hudson-Odoi, Kalimuendo

Emiliano Martinez : The Argentine goalkeeper was sent the wrong way from the spot and could not have saved Jesus' volley but made a couple of other saves. 6

Josh Acheampong : The young defender played within himself at the City Ground. 5

Wesley Fofana : The Frenchman was booed by his own supporters and told he is "not welcome here". It was a tough end to a horrible week which only got worse as he gave away the penalty having first been caught under a long ball. He was substituted in the 56th minute while also on a yellow card. 3

Moises Caicedo : A shock selection to start at centre-back for first time in his 210 games in English football, the Ecuadorian looked out of sorts with possession and in his positioning. He failed to cover for Fofana before he gave away the penalty. 5

Pep Chavarria : The Spanish full-back was an anonymous presence but did not make any obvious mistakes. 5

Romeo Lavia : The Belgian recovered from a poor touch early on to set the tempo for possession domination and his passes had real purpose. 7

Jordan Henderson : The 36-year-old was one of the weaker Chelsea performers as he filled in for now-defender Caicedo. 5

Pedro Neto : The Portuguese winger showed impressive work-rate competing with Williams, while threatened with his running in behind. His second-half shot was blocked but led to Chelsea 's goal, while his cross set up his side's second. 7

Cole Palmer : The forward was creative and highly involved for Chelsea but could not deliver that moment. It owed more to his team-mates not performing than himself. 6

Morgan Rogers : Rogers squandered multiple chances, including a huge opportunity to equalise from a corner midway through the second half. 4

Danny Welbeck : The 35-year-old striker had absolutely no service but was also completely anonymous in the first half and was taken off at the interval. 4

Emmanuel Emegha (on 45, Welbeck): An outstanding second-half display, with a brilliant touch and shot to pull one after the ball deflected into his path. He headed in a second at the far post. It raises the question about why he did not start having also scored against Leeds last weekend. 8

Levi Colwill (on 56, Fofana): The England international will be frustrated to have been dropped for a midfielder but was forced on amid Fofana's struggles and did not have much chance to shine. 5

Subs not used: Penders, Gusto, Barco, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao

The Green Brigade occupy a standing section at Celtic Park

Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.

A Green Brigade statement said the four had been "finally cleared of wrongdoing" over the occurrence, which took place during a game against Falkirk on 29 October last year.

The Scottish champions released footage at the time which they said showed "around 100" supporters verbally abusing and assaulting a steward and two police officers.

The alleged flashpoint came after a ticket inspection at the rail seating section of Celtic Park, the club explained, as they outlined a ban on about 250 supporters, which lasted nearly six months .

The Green Brigade say Celtic's "irresponsible and vindictive claim" was intended to "smear" them.

A statement from the group said: "Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.

"The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed."

Celtic lift suspension of Green Brigade fans group

The Green Brigade called for the club to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with head of security Mark Hargreaves at last year's abandoned annual general meeting .

"This week's outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year," they added.

"It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves' subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives.

"We maintain that Mark Hargreaves has introduced a poisonous security culture to Celtic Park and does not hold the trust of supporters whose safety he is supposed to be responsible for. His position is untenable."

Celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.

The club said: "The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable – it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.

"Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council."

Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a "campaign of personal harassment and abuse" towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.

"Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.

"Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action."

BBC Scotland have contacted Police Scotland for comment.
